MOONFOD

Moon Feature of the Day

A small daily lesson, on a very old world.

Get to know the Moon one landmark at a time: its craters, seas, mountains, and valleys. Each day reveals a feature you can explore on the surface, with priority given to the major landmarks.

Find your way

Swipe left across the Moon for the next day, or right for the previous day. The side arrows do the same thing. Tomorrow’s Moon is available to explore; its lesson arrives tomorrow.

On a touchscreen, tap the Moon or feature name to highlight the outline. Tap the highlighted feature or its name again to open the lesson. There’s no need to double-tap quickly.

With a mouse, hover over the feature or its name to highlight it, then click to read. On a keyboard, use Tab and Enter for controls, Left and Right to change dates, Home to return to today, and Escape to dismiss a lesson or tooltip.

Grounded in real data

The Moon’s phase, sunlight direction, and rotation follow the date. The view is Earth-facing with celestial north up. Brightness is enhanced to make night-side terrain readable; stars are decorative and lunar eclipses aren’t simulated.

Surface imagery: NASA / GSFC / ASU / LROC. Elevation: NASA / GSFC / LOLA. Approximate feature outlines: IAU / USGS Gazetteer. Calculations: Astronomy Engine.

Original code and lesson text are MIT licensed. No account, analytics, or location permission is needed.
